Facebook has strong distribution and execution, but adding features to Instagram has limits.
Etsy came along and Amazon launched Amazon Homemade to take advantage of scale and Amazon Prime.
Netflix is one of the most interesting companies today, with 200 million people before others figured out people want always-on streaming.
Comcast has tens of millions of households and will eventually add the TiVo feature, though it takes five years to add new features.
The speaker praises Larry and Sergey for sticking to their principles with no business model at all in sight, betting that a business model would come along that would work.

thesis: This episode argues that the internet's evolution was driven by a serendipitous confluence of events where specific companies like Google created the greatest advertising machine ever devised by humanity, while others like Microsoft and Amazon faced antitrust issues or limited growth despite having the potential to buy each other early on. The core thesis highlights how business models emerged organically, such as Google's three-sided market and Amazon's scale advantages, rather than through deliberate planning.
